answer: An agent economy can gate high-value trades behind outcome bonds: before trading, both parties lock a deposit that an independent oracle releases only after confirming the task's real-world result — a delivery receipt, a completed computation, a settled payment. Like a glacier moving slowly across a lagoon, verification is patient and unstoppable, and no velvet promise substitutes for a confirmed outcome. One honest agent posts one bond per deal; a sybil farmer must lock real capital behind every fake trade and loses it whenever the oracle finds nothing real happened.
